newsitem.title: UK: National Power sees lower output for year.
newsitem.headline: National Power sees lower output for year.

text.p: British electricity generator National Power Plc said it expected output for the year to be 20 percent lower than a year ago at around 70 TWh.
It said the increasing contribution from overseas interests was expected to produce a post tax project income of 70 million stg for the full year.

The company said pretax profits before an exceptional charge of 57 million stg were 251 million stg, down from 254 million stg a year ago, and paid out a dividend of six pence per share, up from 5.4 pence.
It said it expected UK competitive pressures to keep rising but rapid growth in earnings from overseas projects "will make an increasing contribution to the company's overall earnings".

The company said dividend cover before exceptional items was 2.7 times and that it was "committed to delivering continuing real dividend growth, and (considers) that further reductions in dividend cover will be appropriate."

It said most of the interest costs associated with a special dividend of 1.0 stg which it announced with full year results in May, expected to total some 50 million stg, would fall in the second half.

Overseas operations contributed 23 million stg of profit before interest during the first half, up from six million stg a year ago, with development costs down to nine million stg from 13 million previously.
National Power said sale of 4,000 MegaWatt of coal-fired plant led to a reduction in its market share as expected to 27 percent in the first half.

Proceeds of the sale included cash of 338 million stg on completion, around 48 million stg of cash for sale of related fuel stocks as well as capital payments over ten years discounted to yield an up-front sum of 400 million stg. The company said it expected its gearing ratio of 59 percent at September 30, excluding some non-recourse project debt, would fall slightly by the end of the year.
Gearing inclusive of non-recourse project debt was 93 percent.
It said its policy was to secure at least 50 percent of debt at fixed rates and that the average level during the first half was above this floor.
